Count CNEFE address species on a spatial grid

Source: R/cnefe_counts.R
cnefe_counts.Rd

cnefe_counts() reads CNEFE records for one or more municipalities, assigns each address point to spatial units (either H3 hexagonal cells or user-provided polygons), and returns per-unit counts of COD_ESPECIE as addr_type1 to addr_type8.

Usage

cnefe_counts(
  code_muni = NULL,
  year = 2022,
  polygon_type = lifecycle::deprecated(),
  polygon = NULL,
  crs_output = NULL,
  h3_resolution = 9,
  scope = c("muni", "geom"),
  verbose = TRUE,
  cache = TRUE,
  cache_dir = NULL,
  backend = c("duckdb", "r")
)

Arguments

code_muni

Numeric or character. One or more seven-digit IBGE municipality codes, for example 2927408 or c(2927408, 2919207). Repeated codes are dropped. With several codes, their addresses are counted together (see "Several municipalities").

Required for the H3 grid, which is built from the boundaries of these municipalities. With polygon, it's required under scope = "muni" and ignored under scope = "geom", which finds the municipalities that the polygons intersect (see "Municipalities detected from the polygons").

year

Integer. The CNEFE data year. Currently only 2022 is supported. Defaults to 2022.

polygon_type

The aggregation mode is now inferred from polygon: leave it NULL for an H3 grid, or pass an sf::sf object for user polygons. Passing polygon_type still works and warns.

polygon

An sf::sf object with polygon geometries. When it's supplied, the counts are returned for these polygons instead of an H3 grid. Features with the same geometry as an earlier feature are dropped, with a message, and the first one is kept. Under scope = "muni", a warning reports how many addresses of the municipalities in code_muni fall outside the polygons. When polygons overlap, a warning also reports how many addresses fall in more than one of them, since those are counted in each. If no address falls inside the polygons, the function stops with an error.

crs_output

The CRS for the output object. Only used when polygon is supplied. Default is NULL, which uses the original CRS of the polygon argument. Can be an EPSG code (e.g., 4326, 31983) or any CRS object accepted by sf::st_transform().

h3_resolution

Integer. H3 grid resolution (default: 9). Only used for the H3 grid, so it is ignored when polygon is supplied.

scope

Character. Which CNEFE addresses the function works with. "muni" (the default, and the faster option) uses every address of the municipalities in code_muni. "geom" uses the addresses that fall inside the output geometries (the H3 cells, or the polygons in polygon), whichever municipality they belong to, so the municipalities those geometries reach are read as well. The H3 grid holds the cells whose center falls inside the boundaries of code_muni, plus the neighboring cells that intersect those boundaries. See the section "Border cells at the edge of the region".

verbose

Logical; if TRUE, prints messages and timing information.

cache

Logical. If TRUE (default), the downloaded files are kept in the user cache directory and reused in later calls. These are the CNEFE file of each municipality, stored as a gzipped CSV, and the municipal boundaries used to build the H3 grid or to find the municipalities that the polygons reach, one small file per municipality. If FALSE, temporary files are used and deleted after the call. See clear_cache_muni() and clear_cache_boundaries() to delete the cached files.

cache_dir

Character. Directory to use for cached downloads. If NULL (default), the CNEFETOOLS_CACHE_DIR environment variable is used when it is set, otherwise tools::R_user_dir() with which = "cache". Use this to point large downloads at a secondary drive or a shared volume.

backend

Character. "duckdb" (default) uses DuckDB with the H3 extension, and the spatial extension as well when polygon is supplied. "r" uses h3jsr and sf in R instead, and needs no DuckDB extension for the counts. The municipal boundaries of the H3 grid are still downloaded through DuckDB's httpfs extension the first time, on either backend, and if that fails the simplified geobr boundaries are used instead.

"r" exists for environments where DuckDB extensions cannot be installed, such as some restricted computing clusters. It is not the lighter option: it materializes the filtered address table in R memory, so its footprint grows with the municipality, while DuckDB aggregates in a streaming fashion and stays nearly flat. On São Paulo (5.7 million addresses) the measured peak is about 9 GB under "r" against 0.7 GB under "duckdb", alongside being roughly 13 times slower.

If the constraint is memory rather than installability, keep the DuckDB backend and cap it with the cnefetools.duckdb_config option instead. See ?cnefetools for that option, and the benchmark article at https://pedreirajr.github.io/cnefetools/articles/bench_duckdb.html for the measurements.

Value

An sf::sf object containing:

  • id_hex (when polygon is NULL): H3 cell identifier

  • Original columns from polygon (when polygon is supplied)

  • addr_type1 ... addr_type8: counts per address type

  • geometry: polygon geometry

When polygon is supplied, the output CRS matches the original polygon CRS (or crs_output if specified).

Details

The counts in the columns addr_type1 to addr_type8 correspond to:

  • addr_type1: Private household (Domicílio particular)

  • addr_type2: Collective household (Domicílio coletivo)

  • addr_type3: Agricultural establishment (Estabelecimento agropecuário)

  • addr_type4: Educational establishment (Estabelecimento de ensino)

  • addr_type5: Health establishment (Estabelecimento de saúde)

  • addr_type6: Establishment for other purposes (Estabelecimento de outras finalidades)

  • addr_type7: Building under construction or renovation (Edificação em construção ou reforma)

  • addr_type8: Religious establishment (Estabelecimento religioso)

All eight types are reported. In particular, addr_type7 is retained here, whereas compute_lumi() excludes it when computing land-use mix indices.

Several municipalities

Pass a vector of codes to cover a region that spans more than one municipality. The records of all of them are counted together on one grid built over the union of the boundaries, so every cell appears once.

Calling the function once per municipality and binding the results isn't the same. A cell on a shared border belongs to the grid of both municipalities, so it comes back from both calls, each with only the addresses of its own municipality (under the default scope = "muni"). Counts add up, so those outputs can be combined by summing addr_type1 to addr_type8 by id_hex, but dropping the repeated rows (for example with dplyr::distinct()) loses one side of the border. Shares and indices shouldn't be averaged across municipalities. Compute them from the summed counts, or use compute_lumi() with a vector of codes.

Border cells at the edge of the region

Under the default scope = "muni", only the addresses of the municipalities in code_muni are read. A cell or polygon on the outer edge of the requested area, one that also overlaps a municipality you did not request, therefore describes only the part of it that lies inside the area: its counts leave out the addresses of the neighbor. Adding municipalities moves the edge outward but does not remove it.

Under scope = "geom", the municipalities that the output geometries reach are read too, and every cell or polygon receives all the addresses inside it, so the edge is complete. On the H3 grid, code_muni still defines the grid, and a message lists the neighboring municipalities read to complete it. This costs a download and a read of each of them in full, which is why it is not the default.

Addresses outside the H3 grid

The grid is built from the 2022 IBGE municipal boundaries, at full resolution, plus the ring of cells along them, but each address goes to the cell of its own coordinates. An address geocoded beyond that ring, for example on the coast or on a small island the boundary doesn't follow, lands in a cell outside the grid and isn't counted. A warning reports how many addresses of the municipalities in code_muni this affects, so the counts can be reconciled with their CNEFE totals. Under scope = "geom", the addresses of the neighboring municipalities that fall beyond the grid are expected and not reported.

Municipalities detected from the polygons

When polygon is supplied with scope = "geom", the function finds the municipalities that the polygons intersect, using the 2022 IBGE municipal boundaries, and reads all of their addresses. A message lists them, and a code_muni passed in this case is ignored.

Polygons from another source rarely follow the IBGE boundaries exactly, so a polygon along a municipal border can touch a neighboring municipality by a few meters. That neighbor is then downloaded and read too. The counts are not affected, since only the points inside the polygons are counted, but use scope = "muni" with code_muni whenever you know which municipalities the polygons belong to, which is faster.

See also

compute_lumi() for land-use mix indices on the same spatial units.

# Count addresses per H3 hexagon (resolution 9)
hex_counts <- cnefe_counts(code_muni = 2929057, cache = FALSE)

# Count addresses per user-provided polygon (neighborhoods of Lauro de Freitas-BA)
# Using geobr to download neighborhood boundaries
library(geobr)
nei_ldf <- subset(
  read_neighborhood(year = 2022),
  code_muni == 2919207
)
#> ℹ Using year/date 2022
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpsaIjE9/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.

  polygon = nei_ldf,
  cache = FALSE
)
